Add a local fixed-size-buffer meaning so the visible advice does not open io_uring registration terminology. The borrowed-workbench analogy does not imply C enforces lifetime.

Combine the two lesson cards into one optional reference and remove the quiz calculation card and redundant conversion listing. The visible ideal-model assumptions, code interval, reference dependence and accuracy limits suffice for both questions. The reference supports implementing conversion but is unnecessary for conceptual understanding. Rewritten question 1 tests interval versus exact value in plain language; question 2 already tests fixed bias. Every retained symbol and numerical example was checked.

Combine the lesson timing relationships into one optional reference; remove repetitive substitutions, the host counting listing and quiz calculation card. Visible period, active fraction, fixed-counter comparison, load constraints and board routing support both rewritten prediction questions. Reference equations help later timer configuration but are unnecessary for understanding the waveform. The tap analogy explicitly excludes unlimited power and universal harmless averaging.

Retain the pulse example: its three sample times make missed observation tangible without calculation. All three questions test event retention or receiver diagnosis. Interrupt acceptance, source acknowledgement and finite FIFO capacity stay visible; no equation would improve this objective.

Retain the short C program because unsigned conversion and the due comparison are the mechanism being taught. The less-than-one-cycle observation bound and late-work policy remain outside the mileage analogy. Questions 1 and 3 now test why rollover works and why restarting shifts a schedule; question 2 already tests information lost across missed full cycles. No formula card is needed.

Retain the SDK fragment because the protected copy/clear and restoration of prior state are the objective. The foreground/ISR assumptions, excluded DMA/other core/NMI actors, no-overflow bound and omitted acknowledgement stay visible. All three questions diagnose lost work or choose a valid sharing contract; no maths is required.

Keep one optional wire-time relationship for later estimates; it is useful reference, not required to understand framing overhead. Remove repeated numerical substitutions and the duplicate quiz formula. Ten bit periods, the no-gap assumption, the 100 ms example, electrical compatibility, buffer limits and parsing state are visible. All three questions can be answered with the reference card closed.

Retain the explicit transaction table: the address versus direction distinction is easier to follow than a bit-shift equation. The fictional device contract, seven-bit API parameter, final-read NACK, electrical checks and timeout limitations are visible. All three questions test representation or fault interpretation, without hidden prerequisites.

Retain visible polarity/phase, first-bit readiness and device-specific chip-select timing. Replace mode-number recall with a sampling-edge mismatch diagnosis; the other questions test command exchange order and limits of transfer success. No formula or additional implementation listing is needed.

Retain the observation-choice table and causal investigation sequence: the objective is distinguishing event, data and physical-signal evidence, not calculating a trace cost. All debugger limits, logging interference and watchdog-debug prerequisites remain visible. The three questions diagnose observations and reject unsupported timing conclusions. The source-label wording is clearer, but existing anchor text is protected by glossary.js; this was not a rendered wrong-sense dictionary correction.

Retain the complete 19-line C program because its comparisons, assertion checks and six boundary examples are precisely the behaviour being taught. The invented range and alert threshold are visibly defined; no formula or arithmetic drill is useful. Questions assess boundary selection, scope of host evidence and explicit failure handling. Optional cue cards supply no required facts.

Retain the progress-policy table and reset/recovery explanation. Health evidence and a handled failure are conceptual distinctions; no universal watchdog timeout or numerical calculation can establish them. The three questions correctly diagnose blind ISR refresh, degraded operation and reset planning using visible prerequisites. The monitoring window and device-specific reset/debug behaviour remain explicit.

Retain the three-row scheduling trace because it shows blocked versus ready work and conditional priority preemption directly. A schedulability formula or kernel listing would exceed this introductory selection objective. The three questions require practical scheduling, ownership, capacity and cost decisions. The revised queue source label is a harmless clarification; protected anchor text was never annotated as the bounded-waiting dictionary term.

Retain the complete C model: validation order, persistent state, fault latching and RESET behaviour are the actual objective. The assertion sequence exercises distinct histories and boundary values rather than repeated arithmetic. All state/event definitions and invented range/threshold are visible. Questions predict transitions and distinguish model evidence from hardware evidence; q2 feedback now names the application FAULT state accurately without opening an unrelated OS fault-path definition.

Retain the short shell command and labelled adapter pseudocode because they explain running the preceding model and delivering one terminal result per acquisition. Neither is a gratuitous implementation listing; acceptance values test rules, not calculations. All board limits, failure bounds and recovery requirements remain visible. Questions assess deadline ambiguity, acceptance cases and the actual board workflow; q2 feedback now describes a known test reading without the React controlled-input meaning.

No maths needed for layer responsibilities. The application-library scenario tests allocation of work; the retained bridge question isolates ordinary MAC lookup. The responsibility table and local/end-to-end distinctions supply the prerequisites.

No formula needed: nesting and local Ethernet replacement explain demultiplexing and routing. The revised EtherType question supplies its mapping and the frame question asks why a new frame is needed; retained IPv4 forwarding options follow the explicit no-NAT/no-fragmentation assumptions.

Remove repeated efficiency substitutions; the visible 100-byte/full-frame comparison and explicit frame/IP/wire boundaries suffice. Questions now diagnose omitted gap/preamble and displaced payload; neither needs a memorised byte count or equation.
Retain the bounded Python parser because unpacking and its limits are the objective. No maths. The unchanged question tests what the 14-byte guard proves, with VLAN/FCS/full-frame omissions visible.

No formulas needed for pseudo-header coverage, UDP deployability, MTU and cross-layer effects. The tunnel question now diagnoses the shared outer-IP budget. Retained keys explicitly distinguish ordinary routing, NAT, application proxies and loss mechanisms.

Keep one optional size/rate relationship for later estimation; the prose states both effects and cancellation, and the road-lanes analogy remains optional. Questions test doubling size and rate together and bits versus bytes without requiring arithmetic.

Keep distance/speed as one reference relation, with fibre approximation, route and medium assumptions visible. Questions distinguish travel time from serialization, including a supplied radio/fibre model; removed substitution does not hide prerequisites.

Remove the four-term formula, repeated substitutions and nonessential delay calculator. Visible component definitions and a checked 5.26 ms example support diagnosis; the pipeline question tests concurrency across links, with store-and-forward and overhead assumptions explicit. The pipeline now uses a Markdown timing table with explicit zero-propagation/processing assumptions; the former explicit diagram was not compilable.

Keep only the M/M/1 wait relationship as reference. Poisson/exponential/infinite-buffer/stable-load assumptions and finite means at 50/80/90/99 percent remain visible. The revised question asks why spare service capacity clears bursts slowly, not for a queue calculation.

Keep BDP and the steady window/RTT bound as useful reference choices; payload-rate, feedback-delay and operating-system accounting assumptions are visible. All three questions predict larger flight allowance or diagnose an active receive-window limit.

No equation required after retaining the checked 949/941 Mbit/s ideal ceilings and counting boundary. The revised question tests why retries consume a fixed saturated-link budget; it does not infer a universal TCP loss response.

Remove repeated transfer-time equations. The 20 KB/1 GB comparison states all handshake and timing exclusions; retained multiple-choice scenarios now use reasoning feedback about reuse, lower RTT and TLS setup rather than arithmetic.

Keep one reference card for mapped bits per symbol and raw rate; states, baud, bit rate, noise and overhead are explained visibly. The revised question predicts the benefit and robustness cost of more states, without logarithm recall.

One optional Nyquist relationship earns its place for applying the specified real-low-pass, one-sided bandwidth convention. The visible zero-ISI explanation and 12.4 kbit/s example support the question separating fixed symbol-rate limit from bits per symbol.

Keep capacity and decibel conversion as two reference cards, with AWGN, power/bandwidth, high-SNR and asymptotic assumptions visible. Both questions reason about unchanged channel limits or controlled bandwidth/power comparisons, without substitution.

Remove coding-rate arithmetic cards; visible overhead examples suffice. Retain Manchester code and its unchanged bit trace because code behaviour is the objective. The changed 8b/10b question explains extra transmitted bits; the NRZ clock-recovery caveat remains visible.

No formulas needed. Qualified copper/radio mechanisms and specified reach table remain visible. Retain the cabling and indoor-rate diagnostic keys, with the changed feedback replacing differential-voltage arithmetic by common-mode reasoning.

Keep one optional optical attenuation/power-ratio card; retain visible multiplicative loss, 2.5 percent example and wavelength-specific group index. Rewritten questions distinguish propagation mechanisms and additive dB/multiplicative fractions; reach choice uses specified optics.

Keep frame-rate as one optional reference for capacity planning. Padding, 64/1518-byte boundaries and nominal gap accounting remain visible. Questions now test why ARP is padded and why minimum frames increase processing demand.

No formula required for bit interpretation. Retain the multicast pattern and privacy/allow-list diagnosis, with local/universal administration explicitly distinguished from authentication and proof of randomisation.

Keep random-backoff range and collision round-trip constraint as two useful references; slot/attempt limits and full-duplex distinctions are visible. Revised questions explain collision timing and retry separation; the retained mismatch question is qualified by bidirectional load and implementation.

No maths. Retain short executable switch and source-learning trace because forwarding behaviour is the objective. All unchanged questions isolate normal VLAN forwarding or conditional exhaustion; the code exclusions and TLS limits remain explicit.

No equations needed for tag layout and MTU nesting. Retain interpretation and size-dependent diagnosis questions, with supplied byte counts and command example rather than required recall. Routing, native/voice exceptions and TCP-only MSS limits remain visible.

Retain ARP packing code and field output because constructing/reading the message is the objective; no algebra needed. Unchanged route-selection, request/reply and wrong-mask questions are supported by visible connected/default-route and no-proxy assumptions.

No formula: cache reachability, probes, announcements and shared virtual MAC distinguish failure mechanisms. The unchanged capture-based question establishes stale forwarding rather than inferring it from timing; no universal failover bound is introduced.

No maths needed for trust and scope. Retain ambiguity-aware spoofing evidence and layered-defence questions; the lesson states that encryption protects content but not availability, DAI depends on trusted bindings, and RA Guard is not generic ND inspection.
No equation needed for ordering bridge IDs and tracing a loop. Retained root-election inputs are supplied in the question; loop lifetime is separated from congestion drops and guard limitations.

No formula: the triangle and supplied costs teach actual path choice. Retain the route-comparison question but replace arithmetic-heavy feedback with the role decision; root/designated role versus forwarding state is visible.

No equations: timer values and guarded host-port assumptions are visible. Retain all three practical questions about delayed access, protocol transitions and superior-root protection; no universal recovery guarantee or all-traffic-through-root claim remains.

Keep one reference card for minimum-distance bounds; visible codeword separation and distance-three example explain alternative detection/correction guarantees. Revised nearest-codeword question tests uniqueness; unchanged parity question tests an even-flip blind spot.

Retain runnable checksum because end-around carry and word-order blindness are the objective. No formula needed. Rewritten feedback explains commutativity; both keys preserve alignment assumptions and the wider application/storage checking boundary.

Remove redundant polynomial equations but retain one concrete XOR division and runnable remainder function. The revised question interprets zero residue under the explicitly stated conventions and rejects correction/authenticity overclaims.

No formula card is needed for visible bounded burst/distance guarantees or the qualified random-pattern estimate. Retain CRC-32 code/test vector and the unchanged multi-answer question; protected length, fixed framing and keyless integrity limits are explicit.

Keep one utilisation relationship as optional application reference; frame-plus-propagation cycle assumptions and the checked 0.04 percent example are visible. Revised question asks why the one-outstanding-frame rule idles the link.

Keep one optional ceiling relation for whole-frame sizing. Visible feedback-cycle explanation includes the first transmission and checked 2501-frame example. Revised question predicts why a faster link can require a larger window.

Keep sequence-space bounds as one reference card, with equal SR windows, ordered channels and bounded duplicates stated visibly. Retain supplied Go-Back-N loss trace; revised questions diagnose old/new ambiguity and retained later successes rather than computing window arithmetic.

Keep independent-bit damage and geometric attempts as two useful references with separate assumptions. Visible prose distinguishes raw damage, residual frame loss and elapsed time. Revised multi-answer design question combines FEC, pipelining and selective recovery without a universal throughput formula.

Removal of the IHL×4 and 2^16−1 substitution cards accepted: the unit contrast (IHL in 4-byte words, Total Length in bytes, 65,535 maximum) stays visible in prose and was rechecked against RFC 791. q1 now diagnoses a parser that hard-codes 20 bytes for a 0x46 packet (24-byte header); key and all four distractors verified. Verifier reworded the Total Length bullet/explanation after removing a cross-subject alias.

Short parser kept because reading header bytes is the objective; executed: output fields (version 4, 20-byte header, total length 84, DF set, offset 0, TTL 64, ICMP, 192.168.1.5 → 8.8.8.8) match and the synthetic header checksum sums to 0xffff. TTL subtraction card removed; the 64 → 52 example and its assumptions remain visible. q2 (switches do not decrement; 62) and q10 (observed TTL cannot prove OS or hop count) verified against RFC 791/1812.

Sizing and substitution cards and a fragmenter listing removed; the 4,000-byte example (1,480/1,480/1,020; offsets 0/185/370; wire lengths 1,500/1,500/1,040) and the 980→976 alignment case were recomputed. q4 now diagnoses 980-byte non-final fragments (offset 122.5 unrepresentable); 976/976/28 at offsets 0/122/244 rechecked. q7 unchanged and verified against RFC 791/8200. Van analogy mapping checked; verifier replaced 'higher layer' (linked to a software-architecture term) with 'TCP or the application'.

ID-wrap card removed; 65,536 values ÷ ~15,259 datagrams/s ≈ 4.3 s recomputed. Author's low-confidence 'often tens of seconds' checked: RFC 791 suggests 15 s, RFC 1122 recommends 60–120 s, RFC 8200 uses 60 s, Linux IP_FRAG_TIME 30 s and IPV6_FRAG_TIMEOUT 60 s, so the hedge is supported. RFC 8200 router no-fragment and 1,280-byte rules verified. q11 rewritten to supply the wrap time and test mis-assembly; verifier changed 'higher layer' wording in one explanation.

MSS subtraction card removed; 1,500→1,460 and 1,492→1,452 and the clamp-to-tunnel-MTU mistake verified (RFC 6691/1191). q9 now diagnoses a 1,476 clamp (inner packets 1,516; correct 1,436); all distractors checked. q6 unchanged. Verifier corrected the low-bridge analogy, which said the lorry was 'turned back' (an oversized DF packet is dropped and only the ICMP note returns; the transport resends) and removed 'posted', which linked to HTTP POST.

Lesson unchanged: no maths; ICMP type table, error-suppression rules and traceroute stopping signals rechecked against RFC 792/1122. Questions test interpretation. Verifier reworded only the q12 prompt because 'error handling' linked to a React try/catch entry; the answer key and options are unchanged.

Essential card N = 2^(32 − p) retained and independently judged essential: prefix length versus block size is the module's core relationship; its In words examples (/26 = 64, /25 = 128, /27 = 32, /20 = 4,096) recomputed. Class table and 97% figure rechecked. q2 now predicts the effect of /28 → /29 versus /27 (8/6 and 32/30); verified with ipaddress. Verifier softened the street analogy's 'can reach each other directly' to match the lesson's own caveat.

Three recipe/substitution cards removed; the prose recipe and both boundary tables (192.168.10.64–127, 62 hosts; 172.16.32.0–172.16.47.255, 4,094) were recomputed with Python ipaddress, as were the .33.0/.40.255 ordinary-host examples. q1 (10.20.30.40/27 and .70/27 in different blocks) and q4 (10.4.80.0 assignable in 10.4.64.0/19) verified; every distractor's address classification checked.

One formula card removed; the VLSM table (/25, /26, /27, two /30s, .232–.255 free) and both worked examples recomputed. describe() executed: (172.16.32.0/20, 255.255.240.0, 172.16.47.255, 4094). q10 snippet executed (prints 'error'). q5 (/24 exhausted; /23 = 510 usable), q8, q9 and q11 (/31 .14/.15) verified with ipaddress; q8 and q11 lost only their formula cards.
Lesson and questions unchanged; RFC 1918, RFC 6598 and RFC 3927 (169.254.1.0–169.254.254.255 selectable) ranges rechecked. No maths; no analogy needed for a reference list.

Formula card removed; the 200.10.0.0/22 aggregation and collapse_addresses result (200.10.1.0/24, 200.10.2.0/23, 200.10.4.0/24) executed. q6 now predicts a loop through an over-broad /21 without a discard route; checked against RFC 4632 §5.1 rule 2 and verifier corrected 'should discard' to the RFC's 'must discard'. q7 unchanged and verified with collapse_addresses. Area-code analogy mapping and alignment limit checked.

No maths. Translation table, RFC 4787 REQ-5 (≥2 min UDP, ≥5 min recommended) and RFC 5382 (≥2 h 4 min) rechecked. q1 wording-only change (toy-model wording) verified; q11 unchanged. Switchboard analogy maps public address/ports/translation table and separates filtering from mapping, consistent with RFC 4787.

Only an analogy was added. Author's low-confidence ICE paraphrase checked against RFC 8445 §14 and Appendix B: checks are paced one new transaction every Ta (default 50 ms) and each check sends its first packet before retransmits, so several are in flight. Questions unchanged and verified.

Address-count card removed; 2^128 ≈ 3.4 × 10^38 ('34 followed by 37 zeros') rechecked. New visible facts verified in RFC 8200: routers never fragment (§4.5/§5), Packet Too Big carries the MTU (RFC 4443), 1,280-byte minimum link MTU and the minimal-implementation option of staying within it. Questions unchanged.

Subnet-count card kept as reference with a standalone In words line (/56 = 256, /48 = 65,536, /64 = 1). SLAAC /64 dependence verified: RFC 4862 §5.5.3(d) ignores a prefix when prefix + IID ≠ 128, RFC 2464 §4 requires 64-bit Ethernet SLAAC prefixes. EUI-64 example 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e → 021a:2bff:fe3c:4d5e and q5's 3c → 3e rechecked. Verifier corrected q4's NAT66 explanation and the nat66 glossary entry: RFC 6296 NPTv6 maps addresses 1:1, so it cannot squeeze three subnets into one /64.

Hand-encoding /96 section removed (RFC 6052 forbids the well-known prefix for documentation space anyway). New NAT64/DNS64 walkthrough checked against RFC 6147 (synthesis when no AAAA exists), RFC 6146 (stateful translator with an IPv4 pool) and RFC 6877 (464XLAT for literals). Verifier replaced three 'client-side' phrases that opened a security client-side-code entry.

LPM Python listing removed; the trace table recomputed. New no-match behaviour verified against RFC 1812 §4.3.3.1 (no route at all → Destination Unreachable code 0). q7 now predicts that outcome instead of a Python ValueError; q1 unchanged and verified. Verifier reworded the mail-sorting analogy, whose 'Manchester' and 'M1' opened Manchester-coding and TLS-handshake entries.
Unchanged; Cisco default administrative distances and the select-then-LPM order rechecked. No maths; scenarios already test the two-stage decision.

Only an analogy added (parcel label versus per-leg sticker); the mapping and its limit (TTL/checksum changes, NAT, tunnels, non-Ethernet links) are consistent with RFC 1812 forwarding. Questions unchanged and verified.

Step-bound card removed; at most 32 (IPv4) or 128 (IPv6) bit-consuming steps and O(W) stated in prose with W defined. q9 now predicts lookup-step behaviour as the table grows 1,000 → 1,000,000; verified. q10 and q12 unchanged.

Modulo card kept as reference (14 mod 4 = 2, 14 mod 3 = 2 checked); the four→three 'three of twelve residues keep their path' claim recomputed. Verifier corrected the till analogy: redrawing letter ranges moves many (about half under even ranges), not necessarily most, families, and flow affinity reduces rather than avoids reordering.

Bellman–Ford card kept as essential and independently judged essential: the neighbour rule is the lesson's objective; the worked substitution card was removed and the 9 vs 8 example kept in prose. RIP table (16 = infinity, 30 s, 180 s, UDP 520, 224.0.0.9) rechecked against RFC 2453. q4 lost only its formula card. Signpost analogy checked.
Unchanged; the count-up trace and split horizon/poison reverse limits rechecked against RFC 2453. No maths.

Only an analogy added (shared road atlas). Hello/dead, 224.0.0.5, protocol 89, LSRefreshTime 30 min, DROther Two-Way rule (RFC 2328 §10.4) and Hello parameter mismatch drop (§10.5) rechecked. Questions unchanged.

Cost card kept as reference with a standalone In words line; both cost tables recomputed. q3 now diagnoses why a 1→10 Gbit/s upgrade does not change paths under a 100 Mbit/s reference; q8 lost only its card (1 vs 2, then 1,000 vs 20). Verifier reworded 'lowest total cost', which opened a database query-cost entry. The Cisco 100 Mbit/s default and truncation model are inherited and remain medium confidence.

SPF Python listing and complexity card removed; the Dijkstra trace from A (B1, D3, C4, E7) and q5's trace from E (C3, D4 via C) recomputed by hand. O((V + E) log V) stays as Big-O prose with V and E defined. q5 lost only a reference to the removed code.

Adjacency card kept as reference (10 routers 45 vs 17; 20 routers 190 vs 37 recomputed). DROther Two-Way behaviour verified against RFC 2328 §10.4. q9 now diagnoses 2WAY neighbours as normal; hedged INIT/EXSTART advice is consistent with RFC 2328 state definitions and the §10.6 DD MTU check. Verifier replaced 'Ethernet segment'/'broadcast segment'/'the segment' (opened the TCP segment entry) and linked INIT via 'INIT state'.

ASN-count card removed; 65,536 vs ~4.3 billion and reserved 65535/4294967295 (RFC 7300) and private ranges (RFC 6996) rechecked. Courier-slip analogy maps AS_PATH loop rejection and length preference; its limit (unsigned, prepending) matches RFC 4271 and RFC 6811's scope. q1 unchanged.

KEEPALIVE card removed (90 s hold, one-third interval per RFC 4271 §4.4/§10); full-mesh card kept as reference (100 → 4,950). Base iBGP non-redistribution verified in RFC 4271 §9.2. Verifier aligned the reflector remark with RFC 4456 §7 (a single-RR cluster is a single point of failure) and reworded bare 'hold time' phrases that opened an embedded setup/hold-time entry (lesson table/takeaway and q2).

Python rank() listing removed; the worked LOCAL_PREF example (customer at 300 wins despite prepending) and selection order checked against Cisco's documented algorithm. Supplier analogy mapping and limit checked. Questions unchanged.
Unchanged; Gao–Rexford export table and RFC 7454 /24 and /48 note rechecked. No maths.
Unchanged; dated incident facts retain their earlier sourced verification. No maths.

Two-comparison card removed; the origin and maxLength checks are stated in prose. q9 (192.0.0.0/22 max 23: /24 from 65010 and /23 from 64666 Invalid) recomputed and verified against RFC 6811. Collection-authorisation analogy maps ROA, origin and maxLength correctly ('no smaller than a full van' = no longer than maxLength); its limit matches ROV's origin-only scope. ASPA draft date remains time-sensitive.
Unchanged; 0.0.0.0 → 255.255.255.255 UDP 68/67, DORA order and RFC 5227 probing rechecked against RFC 2131.
Unchanged; parse_options executed (5, 3600) and q7 executed with the lesson function ([53, 55] [1, 3, 6]). 0x0e10 = 3,600 rechecked. Code is the learning objective, so retained.

T1/T2 card and timer listing removed; 12:00/21:00/24:00 and 13:00/16:00/17:00 recomputed. (opened a UX entry). Library-loan analogy checked.
Unchanged; giaddr pool selection, option 82 and snooping limits rechecked. No maths.

modules.title: Transport Layer: TCP & UDP in Depth

lessons.rationale: Range-count card removed: 28,232 (60,999 − 32,768 + 1) and the ports ÷ hold-time model (≈470/s at 60 s) stay visible in prose, both recomputed. q5 now diagnoses which change adds tuples; tested in a Linux 6.12 container that connect() reuses the same 4 ephemeral ports against a second destination and from a second bound source address, and hedged that other OSes allocate differently. Flats analogy: mapping and the full-tuple/reuse limit are accurate.

Both cards (8-byte header; 65,507 = 65,535 − 20 − 8) folded into plain numeric prose (Rule 6). Corrected the Linux oversized-send claim after a container test: the default IP_PMTUDISC_WANT socket fragmented a 60,000-byte datagram into 41 fragments; only IP_PMTUDISC_DO/PROBE returned EMSGSIZE (udp(7)'s 'by default ... EMSGSIZE' wording is outdated). q1 explains header size from services; q2 key (refused or fragmented, all-or-nothing reassembly) holds; 1,480-byte fragment payload checked. Postcard analogy limits (checksum, fragmentation) accurate.

No maths. UDP echo snippet retained (demultiplexing is the objective) and executed on macOS and Linux (b'HELLO'); q4 boundaries 100/200/300 and truncation of an oversized datagram confirmed. Questions unchanged and still answerable. Restaurant analogy: listening socket/accept()/full tuple mapping is fair; limit notes UDP has no accept.

1,232 = 1,280 − 40 − 8 kept as a plain numeric sentence with its path assumptions; card removed. TC-bit retry question unchanged and correct. No analogy: a one-question/one-answer exchange is already concrete; a comparison would repeat the postcard picture from tcp-udp-header.

60 Hz interval card removed; 16.7 ms spacing and ~6 snapshots per 100 ms stay as an illustration. q10 change is workedExample only (formula card → prose, same key). Scoreboard-text analogy maps superseded snapshots and head-of-line blocking; limit covers non-superseded events and media deadlines.

No lesson maths. q9 keeps the forged-source mechanism and states 50 × 100 Mbit/s = 5 Gbit/s in words; every distractor rechecked. Catalogue analogy accurate; the QUIC 3× anti-amplification limit verified in RFC 9000 §8.

Header-length and ISN+1 cards folded into prose (15 × 4 = 60 bytes, 40 for options; 1001/5001 trace). The (N + L) mod 2^32 card is reference: useful, but the visible In words line stands alone. q1/q6 changed only in workedExample; 1301/1302 FIN arithmetic rechecked. No analogy: the numbered trace is the mental model; the next lesson carries the handshake analogy.
No maths, unchanged questions. Phone-line analogy maps the three messages; limit correctly says TCP is not identity proof and must reject old duplicates.

Retry-timing and (A − 1) mod 2^32 cards folded into prose; 1+2+4+8+16 = 31 s and ~63 s match the ip-sysctl tcp_synack_retries text. q7 workedExample-only change rechecked. Analogy corrected: the cloakroom version still stored a coat per customer (per-attempt state), contradicting stateless cookies; rewritten as a stamped ticket that itself carries the party size, with nothing kept at the door.

2 × MSL card folded into prose (4 min with RFC 793's MSL; Linux TCP_TIMEWAIT_LEN 60 s confirmed in v6.12 tcp.h). q4 workedExample-only change. Phone-goodbye analogy kept; fixed 'the side that hung up first' (contradicted staying on the line) to 'said goodbye first'.

No lesson maths. q8 workedExample now reasons in prose: 600 × 60 = 36,000 > 28,232; pool empty after ≈47 s, recomputed. tcp_tw_reuse default 2 rechecked in ip-sysctl. No analogy: the state table and operational checks are procedural; TIME_WAIT already has one in the previous lesson.

No maths. q11 workedExample: 2^32 / 2^16 = 65,536 rechecked; reworded 'next expected number', which opened the DSA expected-value entry. Bank call-back analogy maps the exact-match rule and challenge ACK; limit (on-path attacker, RFC 5961 §7 ACK throttling) accurate.

Last-byte and wrap-time cards folded into prose; 2^32 × 8 / 10^10 ≈ 3.4 s and ≈0.86 s at 40 Gbit/s recomputed. q1 now tests re-segmented retransmission (ACK 6201); q12 tests why fast wrap needs PAWS. Odometer analogy fair; limit notes timestamp wrap and recent-state only.

No maths. rx() executed on Python 3.14 (macOS) and 3.12 (Linux): output matches the lesson and q4 (501/501/1501/2001, 1001 held once). Serial-story analogy maps cumulative ACK/duplicate ACKs; limit mentions bytes and SACK.

Option-length card folded into prose: 2 + 4 × 8 = 34 ≤ 40, five blocks 42, three blocks 26 within the 28 left after timestamps. Questions unchanged. No analogy: the lesson is a short extension of the serial-story picture in the previous unit; another comparison would repeat it.

RTO = SRTT + max(G, 4 RTTVAR) kept essential: it is the RFC 6298 definition the lesson and q5 turn on. EWMA updates are reference with a standalone In words line; 300 → 272.5 ms example recomputed. q5 re-derived by simulation: alternating 98/102 ms settles at ≈108.5 ms, alternating 60/140 ms at 268–273 ms, but evenly spread 60–140 ms samples give only ≈140–200 ms, so the prompt now says the samples alternate and the worked example states that assumption. No analogy: the steady/jittery/slowing-path bullets already give the intuition.

Geometric-sum card removed; 0.3+0.6+1.2+2.4 = 4.5 s and 'each wait exceeds all previous waits' checked. tcp_retries2 15 ≈ 924.6 s (a lower bound), tcp_rto_max_ms 120,000 and rto_min 200 ms checked in ip-sysctl; TCP_USER_TIMEOUT semantics in tcp(7). q7 workedExample-only; q9 diagnoses the backoff signature. No analogy: a concrete capture signature carries the idea.
Summary/reading only changed; no formulas. Questions unchanged and consistent. No analogy: the duplicate-ACK idea is covered by the serial-story analogy two lessons earlier.

PTO = 2 × SRTT card removed; 2 × 40 = 80 ms stated in prose and table (RFC 8985 §7.2). q11 workedExample-only change rechecked against RFC 8985. No analogy: the mechanism table is the clearest summary and the lesson is already dense.

A = max(0, min(rwnd, cwnd) − F) kept essential: the new-data budget is the lesson objective and is needed for q11. lessons.rationale: Frequency/period reciprocals stay in prose; their duplicate card was removed. Wavelength conversion remains a useful physical reference, with units and speed assumptions visible. The question predicts shorter periods without calculation.
Cycle position, radians and cancellation are explained by the table and prose without an equation card. Both questions test unit contracts and phase behaviour; every required conversion is visible.

The sine relationship is the sole essential card because interpreting how its parameters combine is the objective. Angular-frequency conversion is already explicit in prose, so its redundant card was removed. Quarter-cycle output tests parameter meaning.

The two reference cards support oscillator implementation: samples per cycle and phase advance in both units. Visible prose explains their inverse changes, non-integer periods and clock mismatch. All four questions test behaviour rather than substitution.

Wrapped state and preserved phase are the objective, so keep the two short runnable examples and remove glide derivations. The clock-hand analogy maps position versus speed with rounding/slope limits. Questions diagnose resets, numerical spacing and changing-frequency history.

Equal pitch intervals are ratios; doubling and midpoint examples establish the mechanism. Remove the redundant semitone card while retaining its numeric multiplier in prose. Questions compare pitch-space operations rather than recall logarithm identities.

Keep both reference conversions because note-to-frequency synthesis and frequency-to-note tuning need different directions. The compact mapping function and integer-division question teach an actual implementation trap. Tuning convention and display-label assumptions stay visible.

Two cents conversion references serve measuring and applying detune; the beat equation merely repeats frequency-difference prose and was removed. The tuner code makes nearest-note behaviour explicit. Questions predict signed detune and register-dependent beats. Unnecessary secondary hearing thresholds were removed.

Keep one reference card comparing fixed-hertz with fixed-cents control: it documents the implementation distinction. Visible prose supplies the ratio behaviour, pitch-space addition and one-volt-per-octave example. Questions choose consistent units and diagnose register-dependent modulation.

Harmonic order, amplitude recipe and missing fundamental are complete in prose without cards. Questions interpret a supplied close-frequency pair and missing fundamental. Corrected mixing feedback: addition creates no new spectral frequencies but existing components can beat.

Two reference cards support actual callback deadline and memory/data budgeting. Main prose gives the scaling, sample-time meaning and hardware-slot caveat. Questions predict resource changes, keeping arithmetic optional.

The step-size and nearest-rounding bound remain one reference for quantiser design; visible prose and the ruler analogy explain both. Retain the short quantiser trace because rounding versus endpoint saturation is the code objective. All keys match executed code.

Keep the useful SQNR estimate as reference with uniform-error and overload assumptions visible. Executed code tests those assumptions at coarse resolution; removing derivations preserves the failure mechanism. Questions distinguish six-dB-per-bit behaviour, overload and signal level.

No equation is necessary: dither trades noise for removal of correlated error, while measured analogue noise limits converter performance. Questions test this and separate word length, dynamic range and SINAD. Added noiseless nearest-rounding assumptions to the sub-step question.

No cards: the short conversion program demonstrates scaling, rounding and clamping. Question checks float headroom, precision and format boundaries. Corrected feedback so float storage does not promise that every intermediate effect avoids clipping.

Nyquist is explained as a strict boundary and sample ambiguity; no duplicate inequality card remains. The executed sign-inverted-sine example demonstrates the ambiguity. Questions predict rate changes and distinguish ideal reconstruction from plots and aliases.

The wrap/reflection algorithm remains a useful general reference because several sample-rate intervals are possible. The matching short code is the operational objective. Questions trace direction and irrecoverability; phase caveats remain visible.
